paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to carry out of this one. Paul says he and the others serve God "in great endurance; in troubles, hardships, and calamities" (2 Corinthians 6:4). The beatings and the hunger didn't cancel the ministry. They were right there on the list next to purity, kindness and "sincere love" (2 Corinthians 6:6). So a hard season doesn't mean God's work in you has stopped.

Then Paul stacks up those pairs, and they all say the same thing. "Sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; poor, yet making many rich; having nothing, and yet possessing everything" (2 Corinthians 6:10). He isn't pretending the sorrow isn't there. Both are true at once, and the joy doesn't depend on how the day went. I held onto that for a long time in the dark of that junk drawer, and I'm telling you, it holds.

And look at where Paul lands. He sets the list down and says, "Our hearts are open wide" (2 Corinthians 6:11). Then he asks them for a fair exchange, "open wide your hearts also" (2 Corinthians 6:13). Serving God isn't only about enduring. It's about staying open to the people He puts in front of you, even when it costs you. So, baker, who in your life needs you to open up a little wider?
